Pretentious

prih-TEN-shus -- stress on the second syllable, TEN. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pretentious is acting more important, talented, or cultured than one actually is.

The gallery's pretentious brochure described a plain white canvas as 'a conversation with emptiness.'

Worked Example

A classmate returns from one week abroad with a brand-new accent, calls every snack 'cuisine,' and corrects the whole table's pronunciation of 'croissant.'

That performance is pretentious: he is claiming a worldliness one week of travel cannot possibly have given him. Pretentious behavior tries to look grander, smarter, or more cultured than the reality underneath.

How Pretentious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

showy

showy: designed to attract attention in a flashy way

affected

affected: artificial and put on to impress

ostentatious

ostentatious: extravagantly showy to display wealth or importance

Antonyms

unpretentious

unpretentious: modest and genuine, without airs

down-to-earth

down-to-earth: practical, plain, and unpretending

How Strong Is It? — showy → pretentious → ostentatious

showy vs. pretentious

showy vs. pretentious: Showy is the lighter fault -- a showy jacket merely grabs attention, while a pretentious manner makes a false claim, dressing an ordinary person or thing up as something finer than it is.

ostentatious vs. pretentious

ostentatious vs. pretentious: Ostentatious blares even louder than pretentious: a pretentious host drops names and foreign phrases, while an ostentatious one gold-plates the doorknobs and parks the yacht where every guest must walk past it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, in front (Latin prae-)

Root — tent

Root — tent: to stretch; to put forward (from Latin tendere, 'to stretch,' whose past form tentus appears here)

Suffix — -ious

Suffix — -ious: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together

Put it together: Pretentious uses the -ious variant of this unit's suffix family. Pre- ('before, in front,' Latin prae-) + tent ('to stretch; to put forward' — from Latin tendere, whose past form tentus appears here) + -ious ('full of'): Latin praetendere meant to stretch something out in front of you as a claim or excuse. A pretentious person is 'full of' exactly that: claims stretched out for display, held up in front of a much plainer truth.

Use the root in a new word: extend

Use the root in a new word: extend: The library extended its opening hours during exam week.

Root Check

Word Choice

Pretentious always accuses someone of faking it: the grandness on display is not backed by the reality. That is what separates it from fancy -- a genuinely elegant dinner is not pretentious, but calling frozen fish sticks 'artisanal ocean cuisine' is. The related noun is pretension, and 'without pretension' is high praise.
